newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields fall in line with foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields fall in line with foreigners.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell on Tuesday with support from foreign markets with dealers saying a more optimistic assessment of Sweden could explain why the spread against German yields fell a few basis points.
"I think we are watching a fundamental revaluation of Sweden. All key variables look good," one dealer said.
"The spread against Germany could decrease to 80 basis points in a month," James McKay, PaineWebber economist said.
McKay put it down to positive psychology. Even though Sweden has an 'unofficial opt-out', international optimism about EMU still influences Sweden.
A statement by Prime Minister Goran Persson also lent support to the Swedish debt market. He said Sweden must try to take down its debt burden.
Six-month T-bill rates were flat at 4.12 percent while the ten-year bond yield fell seven basis points to 6.69 percent.
The spread between Swedish and German long yields decreased four basis points to 97 basis points.
The crown was stable at 4.4720 against the mark compared to 4.4745 late on Monday.
